articles.title: Does integrin alpha10beta1 enrichment improve cartilage regeneration? Insights from an in vitro and ex vivo human chondral defect repair model.
articles.authors: Ayshath Ruksana C, Aswin M, Parasuraman G, Goyal A, Suresh A, Rebekah G, et al.
articles.study_type: In vitro and ex vivo laboratory study
articles.population: Human chondrocytes from osteoarthritic cartilage
articles.outcomes: Chondrogenic marker expression, hypertrophic markers, matrix production, type II collagen deposition, and cartilage repair scores
articles.take_home: Sorting chondrocytes by integrin alpha10beta1 did not improve cartilage repair compared to unsorted cells, suggesting that this approach alone is not effective for mature chondrocytes. Different strategies, such as scaffold-based approaches or using multiple markers together, may be needed instead.

articles.title: Beyond the Fracture Clinic: 3 Things a Surgeon Can Do to Help Older Patients Stay Out of the Hospital.
articles.authors: Ziebart C, Heckman G, Giangregorio LM, Jiwa F, Thain J
articles.population: Older adults aged 60 years and above undergoing orthopaedic surgery
articles.outcomes: Hospital admissions, falls, fragility fractures, surgical outcomes, intrinsic capacity optimisation
articles.take_home: Orthopaedic surgeons can help older patients avoid hospital admissions by prescribing muscle strengthening and balance exercises, screening for malnutrition and optimising nutrition, and leading bone health improvements. These three simple steps can keep older adults healthier and out of hospital long after their operation.

articles.title: Lateral Femoral Joint-Line Distalization Increases Lateral Collateral Ligament Strain During Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kitchen JM, Richards JA, Powers J, Quesada P, Mont MA, Malkani AL
articles.population: Non-arthritic cadaver knees
articles.outcomes: Lateral collateral ligament strain measured at knee flexion angles of 0, 30, 60, and 90 degrees with progressive lateral femoral joint-line distalization
articles.take_home: Moving the lateral femoral joint-line downward during knee replacement surgery increases strain on the lateral collateral ligament, with significant increases occurring beyond 4 mm of distalization. Excessive distalization may cause ligament damage and contribute to patient dissatisfaction after surgery.

articles.title: Progressive lateral femoral condyle lengthening in total knee arthroplasty produces dose-dependent increases in patellofemoral joint loading and alters patellar tracking.
articles.authors: Shatrov J, Boudali M, Abe K, Parker D, Walter W, Clarke E
articles.study_type: Controlled laboratory study using cadaveric knees
articles.population: Fresh-frozen cadaveric knees
articles.outcomes: Patellofemoral joint reaction force, patellar tracking (translation and rotation), medial and lateral facet loads during passive flexion and stair descent
articles.take_home: Making the outer part of the thighbone longer during knee replacement surgery increases the pressure on the kneecap joint in a dose-dependent way and changes how the kneecap moves. This suggests surgeons should carefully consider how they prepare and align the thighbone component during knee replacement to avoid these effects.

articles.title: Cumulative surgeon volume is associated with improved outcomes following hip arthroscopy: A national registry study.
articles.authors: Holleyman R, Cawley W, Board T, Bankes M, Andrade A, Judge A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome
articles.outcomes: International Hip Outcome Tool (iHOT)-12 and EuroQol-5 Dimensions (EQ-5D) scores at 6 and 12 months after surgery
articles.take_home: Surgeons who performed more hip arthroscopies over time had patients with slightly better functional outcomes at 12 months, but the difference was small and may not be clinically meaningful. High-volume surgeons also tended to treat younger patients with less severe damage, which may have influenced results.

articles.title: Gravity correction and knee isokinetic torque parameters and hamstring-to-quadriceps (H:Q) ratios: reference equations from a large ACL cohort.
articles.authors: Tirosh O, Pranata A, Hartnett N, Hill R, Ganderton C
articles.study_type: Reference equations development and internal validation study
articles.population: Individuals with confirmed anterior cruciate ligament rupture
articles.outcomes: Peak torque values for knee extension and flexion, and hamstring-to-quadriceps ratios, measured with and without gravity correction at three angular velocities
articles.take_home: When measuring knee muscle strength, gravity correction makes a substantial difference to results, with the effect increasing at faster speeds. The study provides equations to convert between the two methods, though the conversion for hamstring-to-quadriceps ratios is less reliable, particularly at higher speeds.

articles.title: Internal versus external femorotibial rotation an anterior cruciate ligament rupture and patellofemoral instability on preoperative standing radiographs.
articles.authors: Chipman DE, Pascual-Leone N, Simpson SK, Matarangas AI, Gross PW, Lijesen E, et al.
articles.population: Children and young people aged 8-21 years with anterior cruciate ligament rupture, patellofemoral instability, or no knee injury (comparison group)
articles.sample_size: 197 patients (60 with ACL rupture, 92 with patellofemoral instability, 45 controls)
articles.outcomes: Femorotibial rotation (internal versus external rotation of the thigh bone relative to the shin bone) measured on three-dimensional reconstructions of standing radiographs
articles.take_home: Young people with ACL rupture tend to have inward rotation of the thigh bone relative to the shin bone, whilst those with patellofemoral instability tend to have outward rotation. These rotational differences were significant and remained so even after accounting for age, sex, weight and leg alignment.

articles.title: Discoid medial meniscus: a systematic review of clinical presentation, surgical management and outcomes.
articles.authors: Akayoglu YK, Sahbat Y, Kose O, Kocaoglu B
articles.study_type: Systematic review of clinical reports and case series
articles.population: Patients with discoid medial meniscus confirmed by imaging or surgery
articles.outcomes: Surgical procedures performed (rim preservation, meniscectomy, repair, allograft); frequency of bilateral involvement, complete morphology, and tears; imaging and treatment patterns over time
articles.take_home: Discoid medial meniscus often affects both knees and usually causes tears, but most patients are treated with surgery that preserves the outer rim rather than removing the meniscus entirely. Recent studies are more likely to use MRI and focus on preserving the meniscus, though better quality evidence is needed to compare different treatments.

articles.title: Femoral elevation variability in direct anterior THA: mechanical assessment of a common table-integrated lift system.
articles.authors: Helgeson EE, Yanamala S, Kelly JJ 4th, Hooke A, Taunton MJ, Nagelli CV, et al.
articles.population: Mizuho OSI Hana traction tables used in hip surgery
articles.outcomes: Femoral lift velocity at different loads (25-100 lb), comparison between left and right lift sides, correlation between table age and lift performance
articles.take_home: Traction table lift speed decreased as weight increased, but all tables successfully lifted the maximum test weight. The tables performed consistently without age-related decline, suggesting mechanical underperformance is unlikely to cause difficulty accessing the hip during direct anterior hip replacement surgery.

articles.title: Total hip arthroplasty in paediatric patients with cerebral palsy: mid- to long-term outcomes of a retrospective cohort.
articles.authors: Stein AM, Mary P, Demoures T, Kabaj R, Vialle R, Gaume M
articles.population: Paediatric patients with cerebral palsy undergoing total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Chronic pain relief, postoperative complications, rehospitalisation within 90 days. Pain relief achieved in most patients; overall complication rate 22% including dislocations, nonunion and loosening; no infections; 13.6% rehospitalised within 3 months
articles.take_home: Hip replacement surgery in young patients with cerebral palsy successfully relieved chronic pain in most cases, with acceptable complication rates over an average follow-up period of 11 years. This suggests the procedure may be a useful option when other treatments have failed in carefully selected young patients.

articles.title: Distal Radial Fracture as an Early Marker of Bone Fragility: A Population-Based Study in Japan.
articles.authors: Shibata R, Sato Y, Tanaka Y
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adults aged 65 to 89 years in Japan
articles.sample_size: 47,178 patients (23,589 matched pairs); 87.8% female, mean age 77.6 years
articles.outcomes: All-cause mortality, secondary fragility fractures, hospitalisation, long-term care deterioration, and osteoporosis treatment initiation
articles.take_home: Distal radial fractures in older adults may indicate skeletal fragility rather than overall weakness, and represent an opportunity to start osteoporosis treatment to prevent future fractures. Patients with these wrist fractures had higher rates of hip fractures afterwards and were more likely to receive osteoporosis treatment within a year.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Fixed-Bearing Lateral Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study With Up to 22-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Tsikopoulos K, Kazamias K, Babis G, Smith JRA, Porteous AJ, White P, et al.
articles.population: Patients with advanced lateral compartment knee osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 113 fixed-bearing lateral unicompartmental knee replacements in 108 patients
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship (primary outcome) and Oxford Knee Score (secondary outcome). Implant survivorship was 97% at 5 years, 93% at 10 years, 89% at 15 years, and 87% at 20 years. Oxford Knee Score improved from mean 17.61 preoperatively to 37.36 at five years post-operation.
articles.take_home: Fixed-bearing lateral unicompartmental knee replacement is a safe and effective treatment for isolated lateral knee osteoarthritis, with very good long-term implant survival and significant improvement in knee function and symptoms. Over 20 years, about 87% of implants remained in place without needing revision surgery.

articles.title: Patient-Defined Outcomes in Arthrosis of the Hip: What Activities Do Patients Hope to Improve with Treatment?
articles.authors: Butler H, Gaddis JM, Mulligan EP, Ma C, Yan J, Wells JE
articles.population: Patients with hip osteoarthritis (Tonnis Grade 2 or 3)
articles.sample_size: 237 patients (91 adults aged 20-60 years, 146 senior adults over 60 years)
articles.outcomes: Patient-defined outcomes (PDOs) regarding hoped-for activity improvements; Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS), International Hip Outcome Tool (iHot 12), and PROMIS Physical Function scores
articles.take_home: Younger adults with hip osteoarthritis hope to return to high-intensity activities like sports and running, whilst older adults prioritise low-intensity activities, but both groups most commonly want to walk without pain. Patient-defined outcomes help doctors and patients agree on what treatment should aim to achieve.

articles.title: Get it moving: Return to activity and sport following primary total knee arthroplasty is not associated with increased adverse events.
articles.authors: Avram GM, Canata GL, Krolikowska A, Hirschmann MT, Becker R, Prill R
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Return to sport; adverse events and implant-related complications
articles.take_home: Returning to sport after knee replacement does not appear to cause more problems with the implant. Most patients can safely do low-impact activities, and some people can return to higher-impact sports with proper rehabilitation and guidance.

articles.title: Osteotomies around the knee are associated with low short-term adverse event and reoperation rates: A 25-year national Hospital Episode Statistics analysis in England.
articles.authors: Hennessy C, Rayes B, Faber BG, Murray J, Abram SGF
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study using national registry data
articles.population: Patients aged 16 to 80 years undergoing high tibial osteotomy or distal femoral osteotomy in NHS hospitals in England over 25 years
articles.sample_size: 24,947 osteotomies in 23,371 patients (mean age 41 years, 62% male)
articles.outcomes: Reoperation rates at 90 days and 1 year; serious medical complications within 90 days including blood clots, heart attack, stroke, kidney injury and infection
articles.take_home: Knee osteotomy is a safe procedure with low rates of complications in the short term: about 2 per cent needed reoperation within 90 days and 7 per cent within a year. Patients with more existing health conditions had higher risks of complications.

articles.title: Patient-reported acceptable symptom state does not reflect quadriceps symmetry 1 year after ACL reconstruction.
articles.authors: Pineda T, Varady NH, Mazy D, Jacquet C, Druel J, Ollivier M
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with anterolateral augmentation
articles.sample_size: 90 consecutive patients (30 each in rectus femoris, quadriceps tendon and hamstrings autograft groups)
articles.outcomes: Agreement between patient-reported acceptable symptom state (PASS) thresholds on KOOS Sport and Quality of Life scales and quadriceps limb symmetry index (LSI) of 90% or more, measured at 12 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: Patient-reported satisfaction with their knee after ACL surgery does not reliably reflect whether their thigh muscle strength has recovered symmetrically. Nearly half of patients who felt their symptoms were acceptable had not yet regained normal quadriceps strength, suggesting that how patients feel and objective strength measurements capture different aspects of recovery and should both be monitored.

articles.title: Medial meniscus posterior root repair with concomitant centralization does not demonstrate superior reduction of meniscal extrusion or improved clinical outcomes compared with isolated repair: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Vasiliadis AV, Gkekas NK, Maris A, Colyvas N, Hantes M
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial meniscus posterior root repair, predominantly female, mean age 50-66 years
articles.sample_size: 309 patients across 6 studies (167 isolated repair, 142 with centralization)
articles.outcomes: Medial meniscus extrusion measured by MRI, Lysholm score, International Knee Documentation Committee score, visual analogue scale pain scores
articles.take_home: Adding a centralization procedure to medial meniscus posterior root repair does not meaningfully reduce meniscus bulging or improve patient outcomes compared with repair alone. The small difference in extrusion between groups (0.6 mm) is unlikely to be clinically important.

articles.title: Do Patients Who Have Medicare Advantage Have Differing Lengths of Stay Following Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Procedures Compared to Traditional Medicare?
articles.authors: Wright AL, Parisi ZJ, Stambough JB, Siegel ER, Mears SC, Barnes CL, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip and knee arthroplasty with Traditional Medicare or Medicare Advantage coverage
articles.outcomes: Length of stay in hospital; discharge disposition
articles.take_home: Patients with Medicare Advantage insurance stayed slightly longer in hospital after elective hip and knee surgery compared to those with Traditional Medicare (1.58 versus 1.37 days), but there was no difference for emergency procedures. Where patients were discharged to after surgery had a significant influence on length of stay.

articles.title: Pregnancy, Sexuality, and Total Hip Arthroplasty: Experiences of Women Younger than 45 Years.
articles.authors: Ozdemir E, Leneman MR, van der Voort NPAN, Visser J, Rijnen WHC
articles.population: Women aged 14 to 44 years who underwent total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 132 women responding (42% response rate) with 168 total hip replacements and 188 pregnancies
articles.outcomes: Pregnancy outcomes (vaginal delivery vs caesarean section), hip pain during pregnancy, sexual satisfaction before and after surgery
articles.take_home: Young women can safely have vaginal deliveries after hip replacement, with most pregnancies progressing without major complications. Sexual satisfaction improved for nearly half of women after surgery due to reduced pain and better mobility.

articles.title: Intercondylar notch width index and graft failure after ACL reconstruction: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Nicholas PRM, Ulla S, Rankin CS, Young D, Davidson L, Spencer SJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Graft failure, defined as need for revision surgery. Interobserver reliability of notch width measurements. Association between notch width index, patient age, graft diameter and graft failure.
articles.take_home: The width of the space in the knee bone where the ligament sits was not linked to whether the reconstructed ligament failed. Younger patients and those who received smaller grafts were more likely to need revision surgery, suggesting that using appropriately sized grafts and considering additional supporting procedures may help reduce failure risk in higher-risk patients.

articles.title: Functional outcomes of patient-specific instrumentation versus conventional instrumentation for unicompartmental knee replacement: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Ruhle V, Rudran B, Leung B, Merle C, Murray D, Price A, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary unicompartmental knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Score at 1 year, Knee Society Score, Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, revision rates
articles.take_home: Patient-specific instrumentation for partial knee replacement did not produce better functional outcomes than conventional methods. Both approaches gave similar results in terms of pain, function and satisfaction after surgery.

articles.title: Anterior cruciate ligament resection has no clinical effect on mediolateral gap laxity assessment in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Leggieri F, Grant S, Wood JA, Sergis N, Wernecke GC, Chen DB, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Mediolateral laxity gap measurements in extension and flexion before and after anterior cruciate ligament resection
articles.take_home: Removing the anterior cruciate ligament during robotic-assisted knee replacement does not meaningfully change measurements used to position the implants. This suggests surgeons do not need to remove it routinely just to get accurate alignment measurements.

articles.title: Graded Association Between Preoperative Bone Mineral Density and Two-Year Postoperative Complications After Primary Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Chen WC, Shen PH, Wu CC, Pan RY, Lin LC, Wang SH
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip or knee arthroplasty with preoperative bone density scans
articles.outcomes: Reoperation within two years, periprosthetic fracture, infection, readmission, mortality, and dislocation
articles.take_home: Patients with weaker bones (osteopenia or osteoporosis) had higher rates of needing further surgery within two years of hip or knee replacement compared to those with normal bone density. The risk increased gradually as bone density decreased, suggesting that even mild bone weakness may increase complication risk.

articles.title: Collared, Uncemented Stems Markedly Reduce Periprosthetic Femoral Fracture Risk in Women >/= 70 Years: A Swiss National Registry Study.
articles.authors: Ladurner A, Kramer M, Giesinger K, Zdravkovic V
articles.population: Women aged 70 years and older undergoing uncemented total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery for periprosthetic femoral fracture
articles.take_home: Uncemented hip implants with a collar design significantly reduce the risk of femoral fractures in women aged 70 and over compared to collarless designs. Other design features such as offset and neck-shaft angle did not affect fracture risk.

articles.title: Delayed Initiation of Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin Chemoprophylaxis Is Associated with Higher Risk of In-Hospital Screen-Detected Distal Deep Vein Thrombosis Following Hip Fracture Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Hou W, Han Z, Kong J, Dong Q, Zhang Y, Feng X
articles.population: Patients aged 55 to 99 years (mean 72) undergoing hip fracture arthroplasty with perioperative low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis
articles.outcomes: Screen-detected in-hospital venous thromboembolism, distal deep vein thrombosis, proximal deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
articles.take_home: Delaying blood clot prevention treatment for 19 hours or more after hospital admission increased the risk of distal deep vein thrombosis following hip fracture surgery, with each hour of delay raising risk by 0.3%. There was no clear link between delay and more serious blood clots affecting larger vessels or the lungs.

articles.title: Effect of Dementia on Risk Factors for Postoperative Delirium in Older Patients Undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on a Large National Dataset.
articles.authors: Lin HL, Lu HT, Lee CY, Chang CY, Lin ES, Lin HC
articles.population: Patients aged 75 years and older undergoing primary or revision total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative delirium incidence and risk factors, stratified by dementia status
articles.take_home: Patients with dementia had a much higher rate of delirium after knee replacement surgery (20.7% versus 2.6%) and dementia was an independent strong risk factor. Different factors predicted delirium in patients with and without dementia, suggesting that cognitive screening before surgery may help identify those at highest risk.

articles.title: Outpatient and Early Discharge Revision Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Pooled Quantitative Analysis.
articles.authors: Hiatt JL, Ricciardelli ZM, Schwab JM, Baker CC, DeCook CA, Naylor BH
articles.study_type: Systematic review and pooled quantitative analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee arthroplasty or revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 14 studies identified; 11 eligible for quantitative synthesis
articles.outcomes: Medical complication rates, periprosthetic joint infection, transfusion rates, patient selection factors (BMI, comorbidity index, ASA class)
articles.take_home: Outpatient revision knee and hip replacements appear safe in carefully selected healthier patients with simpler procedures, with similar or lower complication rates than hospital admission. Patient selection by surgeons is important to ensure good outcomes.

articles.title: Does the Timing of Antibiotic Administration Affect Culture Results During Resection for Periprosthetic Joint Infection?
articles.authors: Graham S, Pinski J, Hietpas K, Metcalf R, Rowe T, Odum S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing staged treatment for periprosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Culture discordance rates between preoperative aspiration and resection cultures; reimplantation success rates
articles.take_home: Giving antibiotics before surgery to remove an infected joint replacement may make it harder to identify the correct bacteria causing the infection and leads to more failed treatments. Waiting to give antibiotics until after cultures are taken appears to improve results.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors for Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Patients Undergoing Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty Who have a History of Surgically Treated Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Another Joint.
articles.authors: Constantinescu D, Graham S, Dombrowsky A, Chandler C, Hietpas K, Otero JE
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip or knee arthroplasty who had previous surgically treated prosthetic joint infection in another joint
articles.outcomes: Incidence of prosthetic joint infection after primary arthroplasty, evaluated by prior treatment strategy and patient factors
articles.take_home: Patients with a history of treated joint infection can safely have another joint replacement with a low infection risk (1.5% at one year) similar to patients without prior infection, provided they are medically optimised beforehand. Those who previously had joint replacement surgery with exchange procedures had slightly higher infection risk than those treated with antibiotics and implant retention.

articles.title: Z-Codes as a Social Determinants of Health Screening Tool for Perioperative Risk Stratification in Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Thota PK, Pondugula P, Pandya S, Sheth NP
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty with minimum two-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection, revision surgery, emergency department visits, readmission, acute kidney injury, and periprosthetic fractures at 90 days, one year, and two years
articles.take_home: Patients with documented social determinants of health had higher rates of complications after hip replacement, particularly infection, revision surgery, and fractures emerging over two years. Using Z-codes to identify these patients may help surgeons provide closer monitoring and support after surgery.

articles.title: Seiza Sitting After Total Hip Arthroplasty: Patient-Reported Outcomes and Three-Dimensional Kinematic Analysis.
articles.authors: Nakao Y, Hamai S, Kawahara S, Ikebe S, Higaki H, Nakashima Y
articles.study_type: Mixed methods study: questionnaire survey with 3D kinematic analysis
articles.population: Patients who had primary total hip replacement surgery
articles.sample_size: 431 questionnaire respondents from 725 patients; 52 patients (74 hips) underwent kinematic analysis
articles.outcomes: Ability to perform Seiza sitting after surgery, reasons for avoidance, hip and pelvic movement patterns, risk of implant contact during the activity
articles.take_home: About half of patients could perform Seiza sitting easily after hip replacement, and 58% regained the ability overall. The movements involved in Seiza sitting appear safe with no risk of implant parts touching, but many patients avoid it due to worry about hip dislocation rather than actual physical limitations.

articles.title: Determination of an Intraosseous Safe Corridor for Suprapubic Screw Placement in Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Bauer J, Brocke D, Peterson A, Beshay Y, Singh R, Rajan R, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Definition of safe corridor angles for suprapubic screw placement in sagittal and axial planes using anatomical landmarks
articles.take_home: Researchers identified specific anatomical safe zones in the pelvic bone for placing supplemental screws during hip replacement surgery, using landmarks such as the anterior superior iliac spine and acetabular rim to guide placement. These findings provide practical guidance for surgeons, though further validation is needed for more complex cases.

articles.title: Excellent 10-Year Implant Survivorship Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients Who Have Down Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Shafau AL, Elnaggar A, Almaat A, Jaume A, Darwiche H
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients with Down syndrome undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty, compared to matched patients without Down syndrome
articles.sample_size: 255 patients with Down syndrome (mean age 43 years); 246 matched controls
articles.outcomes: 10-year revision-free survival, mechanical failure-free survival, freedom from subsequent hip or pelvic surgery, and comparison of complication rates between groups
articles.take_home: Hip replacements in people with Down syndrome showed excellent long-term results, with 94.6% of implants still functioning at 10 years without revision surgery. The outcomes were similar to people without Down syndrome, suggesting that Down syndrome alone does not affect how well hip replacements work.

articles.title: Analyzing 30-Day Episode Costs for Total Joint Arthroplasty: Identifying Targets for Cost Reduction Under Bundled Payment Models.
articles.authors: Olatunbosun S, Playter K, Hollenbeck B
articles.population: Commercially managed Medicare patients who underwent lower extremity joint arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 30-day episode of care costs, breakdown of costs by hospitalization, readmission, home health and skilled nursing facility services
articles.take_home: Total joint arthroplasty costs averaged between £21,000 and £34,000 in the first 30 days after discharge, depending on patient complexity. The biggest opportunities to reduce costs are preventing readmissions and managing post-discharge care in nursing facilities.

articles.title: Postoperative Hip Function as a Predictor of the Forgotten Joint Score-12 at One Year Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Wada O, Nagai K, Igeta M, Mori A, Mizuno K
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Forgotten Joint Score-12 at 12 months postoperatively; hip range of motion, quadriceps muscle strength, pain, and perceived leg-length discrepancy at 3 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: Better hip movement, stronger thigh muscles, and lower pain at three months after hip replacement surgery were linked to patients being less aware of their new joint at one year. Early rehabilitation focusing on movement, strength, and pain control may help achieve this.

articles.title: Diabetes is Associated with an Increased Risk of Arthrofibrosis Following Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Hall RP, Braithwaite CL, Van Schuyver PR, Verhey JT, Lebens R, Deckey DG, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Arthrofibrosis requiring manipulation under anesthesia or arthroscopic lysis of adhesions within three months, three to 12 months, and over 12 months after surgery
articles.take_home: Patients with diabetes had a higher risk of stiffness after knee replacement surgery within three months, with worse blood sugar control associated with greater risk. This increased risk was mainly seen in the first three months after surgery.

articles.title: Tourniquet Use Independently Predicts Early Quadriceps Inhibition Following Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Dose-Response Analysis.
articles.authors: Altun O, Dasar U, Bozkurt M
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Quadriceps muscle inhibition measured by ability to perform active straight leg raise on postoperative days one and three
articles.take_home: Using a tourniquet during knee replacement surgery was linked to more quadriceps weakness in the early recovery period, with longer tourniquet use associated with greater weakness. Higher body weight and longer surgery time also increased the risk of this weakness.

articles.title: Aortic Stenosis and Total Hip Arthroplasty Complications: The Role of Perioperative Medications.
articles.authors: Hwang J, Wei R, Valencia A, Sambandam S
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adults undergoing total hip arthroplasty, with and without aortic stenosis
articles.sample_size: 7,582 patients in each matched cohort (15,164 total)
articles.outcomes: 30-day complications including stroke, myocardial infarction, transfusion, pneumonia, acute kidney injury, intensive care admission and readmission
articles.take_home: Patients with aortic stenosis having hip replacement surgery have higher risks of stroke, heart attacks and other complications within 30 days compared to those without aortic stenosis. Using tranexamic acid on the day of surgery reduced the need for blood transfusions and intensive care, but certain heart medications taken on surgery day were linked to increased stroke risk.

articles.title: Tibiofemoral rotation in patellofemoral pathology: a systematic review of imaging modalities, measurement techniques and clinical relevance.
articles.authors: Tan GJS, Desai RM, Patil A, Mandalia V
articles.population: Studies assessing tibiofemoral rotation in patellofemoral instability or anterior knee pain
articles.outcomes: Tibiofemoral rotation values measured by imaging, association with patellar maltracking, recurrent instability and knee pain
articles.take_home: Increased outward rotation of the tibia relative to the femur is linked to kneecap problems and recurrent instability, but measurements vary widely depending on the imaging method and technique used, so this measurement cannot yet be reliably used to guide routine clinical treatment decisions.
